newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil sold down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil sold down sharply.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps came under strong selling pressure late afternoon on Wednesday losing more then $1.00 per barrel in active trading as sellers came out in force triggered by offers from majors, traders said.
"Gas oil just collapsed after some majors came out to sell which spooked an already weak market," a trader said.

July swaps were last quoted at $19.80/$20.00 per barrel down from Tuesday's $20.90/$21.00, brokers said. July traded earlier in the day at $20.68 and $20.70, and in the afternoon at $20.30 and $20.00, they said.

August was also down sharply at $20.80/$21.00 from Tuesday's $21.60/$21.80, with deals done in the morning at $21.70 and $21.65 and in the afternoon down to a low of $20.50 before rebounding slightly, brokers said.
They said about one million August barrels exchanged hands in hectic afternoon trade.
Traders said the slump in prices were due to expectations of sustained aggressive physical offers for the rest of the week at least, amid poor regional demand which has led to high stocks.
On Tuesday, July gas oil was offered to a low of $20.80 per barrel, down 50 cents from Tuesday's lowest offered level.
"Gas oil was offered below $21.00 for the first time in over a year but still no one was interested in buying. The market is quite depressed," a trader said.
Gas oil prices, at their lowest level since October 1995, are expected to come off further because big regional buyers such as China and India are not buying large volumes.
India's unexpectedly low 165,000-tonne award for August delivery cargoes on Monday compared to the 855,000 tonnes awarded for July initiated the sell off, traders said.
China, facing high domestic stocks, are still not in the market to buy large volumes for third quarter arrival.
Abundant supplies in the MidEast could see cargoes coming this way in August, adding on to high stocks in Singapore and South Korea.
Fuel oil is steady following earlier fresh physical support from a local trader who on Monday bought two 20,000-tonne cargoes at $99.00 per tonne.
August and September swaps were quoted at $98.75/$99.50 per tonne, brokers said.
